how: Public appeals recruit people to make and defend a flag, a heart and other Polish pictures.
Participants judge maintenance capacity and whether two placers can make a heart recognisable before others treat it as vandalism.
A member proposes the flag that becomes the object of subsequent coordinate-setting and guarding, without establishing why each later placer joined.
Participants propose national pictures and revise lettering while preserving disagreement over which version to build.
A participant reports a repaired pixel while describing continuing attempts to alter the flag.
Coordinates and templates turn picture proposals into specific work that participants can attempt.
A request for restraint receives bare assent, and a shared-defence proposal receives a short commitment to try.

statement: Routing current plans and participants into a separate chat.
how: Participants route builders and questions about current plans into chat and pinned instructions.
When plans are routed into chat, a participant without chat access limits contributions to conservation.
Script recommendations, bot links and permission talk establish tool mobilisation but require evidence of execution before they establish automated placement.
Retrospective references to leaders and command put this room on the claim's discussed-order side without establishing appointment procedures or general enforceability.
Guarding, warnings and repair keep an alterable flag and eagle in place while participants dispute expansion.
A participant deliberately spoils the flag and reports that someone repairs the change within five seconds.
Participants distinguish coordinated activity from spontaneous expansion and disown attacks attributed to outsiders.
A proposal to publish suspected placers' names meets an anti-witch-hunt rule and is redefined as a list for recruiting future diversions.
Retrospective speakers assign credit to allies, leaders or disobedient placers, leaving the competing attributions unresolved.
Visitors and residents negotiate restraint, assistance and compromises over overlapping pictures.
Participants propose going around neighbouring art, respect a ceasefire, refuse an attack and apologise for damage attributed to other placers.
Participants offer reciprocal assistance, report repairing a neighbour's logo and exchange greetings or requests for help.
Participants recount mutual defence in a larger coalition and credit several allies with survival they could not individually secure.
A member supplies Polish wording for another group's chat negotiations without thereby acquiring authority over every placer.
Acceptance of a reciprocal offer immediately disclaims authority to speak for every member of the national community.
References to pictures on the flag and resentment of command do not establish guests' subjection to a host's approval rules.
A proposal to draw lower around a resistant neighbour does not document completed relocation after the work was erased or overrun.
A surviving title calls for taking over another country's canvas space without documenting the attack's execution.
Members propose consuming neighbouring pictures, adding a swastika and annihilating nearby logos as a defensive buffer.
A member reports deliberately spoiling the national flag, demonstrating that destructive action can originate within its apparent constituency.
An ultimatum to a neighbour receives a refusal, carrying the dispute in reciprocal talk without proving a physical attack.
Members announce success, thank participants for shared play and appreciate avoiding war with a neighbour.
Participants recount a mock battle history and mourn a neighbouring inscription consumed by the flag before placement ends.
After closure, members dispute the retained account of who made the result through competing claims about leaders, allies and disobedient placers.
A participant proposes organising earlier and choosing a funny shared design for another occasion.
A late post shares a replacement canvas without establishing that anyone adopts it.
Renewing shared activity can mean a themed meme day, whose proposal elicits reminders of the recent canvas flood and possible participant fatigue.
Members investigate missing voting arrows, enact a quotation game and judge familiar pranks within the host's separate April Fools conduct.
A shared joking frame can contain disagreement within moderation and an organiser's withdrawal, so it does not establish unanimous consent to the joke.
Members propose one general thread, deletion of separate canvas posts, a megathread and a filterable tag in response to crowded discussion.
Boundary proposals remain disputed and can be withdrawn when the event's short duration becomes known, so proposals cannot establish an implemented removal policy.
Participants argue whether pixel-taking is nationalism and whether recolouring a rainbow is destruction or play, without arriving at one shared political reading.
An attack proposal names national history in its own wording without establishing a pre-existing personal or inter-room quarrel.
Historical attack language does not establish that these participants carried an actual pre-canvas quarrel into the event.

statement: Soliciting evaluation of a canvas image whose substantive object cannot be recovered from the coded passage.
how: The surviving invitation to give an opinion is observable, but the inaccessible image leaves its organising object and consequence unresolved.
Calls and later repair reports do not identify which call caused a member to join or perform that work.
The initial proposal is itself a call, leaving a separate starter-to-recruitment mechanism unestablished.
Upkeep overlaps achievement because reporting a flag as made does not remove the continuing need to repair overwrites.
A participant explicitly connects the flag's inevitable encounter with neighbours to the question of reaching agreement.
An announced ceasefire is explicitly offered as a reason to respect the neighbour's work.
Treaty-based restraint reaches only participating placers because acceptance disclaims universal authority and unaligned people can keep overwriting protected work.
Maintenance pressure and tool circulation coexist without a coded passage linking manual overload to actual automated deployment.
Reporting completion and celebrating it can occur in one turn rather than as separate successive stages.
Celebration and recording are visible, but remembering during ongoing placement does not establish that celebration prompted preservation.
A final-image announcement, another-activity proposal and clone offer do not establish that recording caused continuation or that continuation was adopted.
Capacity doubts do not document a subsequent decision to abandon a spot and relocate.
Template provision settles design only with shared acceptance because a template request and competing letter configurations do not establish agreement.
A proposal to test cooperation against a shared threat receives a short commitment to try, without demonstrating an obligation for every reader to answer.
A shortage-based appeal and later testimony of allied help do not recover the specific recruitment and delivery mechanism between them.
A reciprocal offer is accepted and a participant reports repairing the neighbour's logo in the same negotiation.
Recruitment and attack proposals do not establish that recruited hands were redirected by the original call.
Attack proposals receive both a bare refusal with a chat invite and a reasoned appeal to joint defence.
Attack refusals invoke common defence or redirect participants without documenting a new negotiated settlement produced by an attack call.
An ultimatum sustains contest in talk without evidence of an executed attack, so this transition must not imply observed pixel damage.
Coalition survival is a participant's retrospective explanation, while the timing and decisions that produced alliance membership remain outside these concepts.
The complaint explicitly connects a page full of canvas posts with the request for one general discussion thread.
A proposed deal receives acceptance immediately qualified by the speaker's inability to bind every member.
